Author: @risac.8384
Content: FFFF - ‘Keep Up.’ The writing in this game! I went through a life or death fight with my health and got a second chance at life. Damn did they capture this beautifully- because I’d absolutely give that away to save someone like that. Especially how Chase and Robert are chosen family - and how that plays into the dynamic with Invisigal. Chase is angry seeing her influence/connection to someone he loves and the stress it’s causing. However he recognizes a person worth saving, especially for his chosen family. The pacing of the scene is also telling, because the eye contact and choice of wording speak volumes. It’s not just a play on how fast Chase is, it’s also him trusting Robert to follow through and make sure whatever the sacrifice isn’t in vain. That’s that family, chosen or otherwise, level of trust where both people are needed to complete something and can trust the other to come through - even with a split second understanding. Chase knew Robert would track him, and Invisigal, then follow through on whatever happened (whether that’s saving her life or saving both their lives as urgent healthcare would be needed in either or both cases). Beautiful writing 🥰

Damn I actually think either Invisigal or Blonde Blazer is a mole. BB is the easiest to explain: she is in the right position to sabotage the repairs on Mecha Man, she could have given the location to Shroud after convincing the team to not go. Also general vibes.

Also, would Shroud nearly kill Invisigal if she was a double agent, just to keep her cover?

I feel like we still need a lot of evidence to claim anything, but that's the evidence places out. Visi and Blonde could just be red herrings too, which is fun, but still leaves the question as to who'd the traitor.

Content:
It's 3:57 a.m. right now, and I just had a realization. What if Chase planted the bomb on Mecha Man's back and was working with Shroud? I believe it's Chase because he's the only one who shows a debuff or side effect when using his superpowers. First, we don't see the bomb on Mecha Man's back until Robert gets a warning about it. When Mecha Man blasts off like Team Rocket, Chase could run, jump on his back, plant the bomb, and jump off instantly. We saw how fast Chase can move, so it's understandable why we didn't see the bomb earlier. My second reason?

Author: @larrywalsh9939
Content:
I love this game, the writing's awesome, but there's a few points that bug me. For example, he keeps getting into fights and keeps taking a beating, he's always got bruises all over him, but his face always heals in seconds. 

Mecha Man holds a press conference, saying he's stepping down from superhero work - and even if people had never seen him out of the suit before, they could see him there - scrawny little guy with a gravelly voice. Immediately after, SDN gets a new dispatcher, you know, guy who used to be a hero, scrawny little guy with a gravelly voice, no idea who HE could be. That's a disguise right up there with Clark Kent glasses. 

People speak highly of Mecha Man, who goes into combat in a flying tank with guns, lasers, a lightsaber, shields, etc etc. Now granted, I'm no big beefy dude, but if you put me in a wrestling ring up against Andre the Giant and I show up in an Abrams M1A1 tank, well, that doesn't look courageous. It looks mismatched, and yeah, of course I won, I drove a tank into the wrestling ring.

I love how the lamps everyone brought fit them in one way or another:

Punch Up brought a short lamp the same colors as his outfit.
Prism's lamp appears to have multiple brightness levels, because Prism controls light rays.
Waterboy and Phenomaman's lamps correspond to their starting stats. Herm's lava lamp is dim; Dumpy's floodlight is too bright for Rob's apartment.
Golem's salt lamp, like him, is made of earthen materials.
Flambae put a CFL in his lamp. CFLs are hotter than the LEDs everyone else's probably had.

Content:
Fun fact. Chase says in Episode 1 that he runs at 50x the speed of an unpowered human. I did the maths. If he was running at 50x a Marathon runner's speed (about 13mph, or 21kph) he'd be going at 650mph or over 1000kph. That's basically 1 mile every 6 seconds or so. He could cover the distance between London and Inverness in under 1 hour, and not be particularly out of breath, if we treat him like a Marathon runner (which would make sense considering his name, Track Star).

On the other hand, if he's running at 50x an Olympic Sprinter's speed (20mph or 32kph), he'd be going 1000mph or 1,600kph. That's even more insane. That'd be 1 mile every 3.5 seconds or so. Thought you'd find this bit of maths interesting, for just how awesome Chase is. Keep up.

Author: @Buddy_Beatz
Content:
Don't know If i was the only person to do this. (I doubt it, little bit a strategy would bring you do this conclusion) BUT. I evened out all my hero's points. So I pretty much have everyone at 3-4 in every skill. that way i can literally send ANYONE to any job, The reason i did that. I kept sonar, and since he flips his charisma and intellect to vigor and combat; I wanted to make sure that no matter what form he was in he could do well on whatever job (as he was my only good charisma and intellect at the time). so I started trying to make him 4 4 1 4 4, then got to say 3 on combat and vigor and thought "what if i did this to everyone". Now everyone is pretty high level for me and almost everyone has 4 in every skill with some having a couple of 5's. If i send ANY 3 heroes on a job i fill the whole board with 10s. Even Waterboy for me right now is 3-4's all round, and that healing 2 others ability is a godsend.

Works out very well. also allows you to keep leveling up everyone easier and evenly cus you can send them to whatever. You do have to send 2 heroes quite often, BUT their abilities often make up for that. high level synergies of heroes in pairs of 2 often result in an insta win as well. I didnt even have the gray covered completely and got buffed from like an 84% to a 98% chance of success. I know its hard to lose and 84 but even harder to lose a 98. 

Hope that helps someone!!!

Author: @saransharora9357
Content:
I don't think anyone on the team is the mole. There are way too many red herrings and I think the devs want us to suspect everyone over this 1 week. It'll probably tear the team apart in the next episode. Blazer asking to delay the hit, Coupe being alone on her phone in the balcony, Prism recording the fight, Waterboy going to the bathroom right after Robert tells him something about the plan, Royd's proximity to the mecha man project, Flambae's backstory with mecha man etc etc. It would be too obvious, I think, to have someone blamed for an intentional or unintentional leak. Instead, I think the mole is the work computer.
Hear me out, its subtle enough to seem obvious in hindsight but its also very incognito in the high tension scene in the apartment. Exactly something I could see the devs trying to pull off. More importantly, there was also the hack a day before which says "red ring influence detected" and Galen says at 1:26:41, the next day, that someone might have gotten into their secure servers. So Shroud might have listened in to their entire conversation in the apartment and on mission through the computer and that's how he is always one step ahead. That's my best bet. If not, I would give a shout out to Galen with his super hearing and the same subtlety thing but he doesn't have much else in the way of concrete evidence.

Author: @Solid_Sayori
Content:
Okay, my biggest criticism of the game, despite the fact that it is genuinely well written, is the stupid illusion of choice crap. I get that AdHoc doesn't have the money to make Baldur's Gate 3 or Detroit: Become Human, in terms of branching narratives. But even while I am watching just your playthrough of the game, it is painfully obvious that most of the choices are just flavor choices. 

Sonar or Coupe? Well you fire one, someone else gets pissed off at you for an episode, and then everyone acts like nothing happened (and NO ONE calls out Blondie for being a terrible boss). Side with Invisigal or Blonde Blazer in episode 6? Doesn't matter, Chase chews out Invisigal, she hits him, and then Invisigal goes to the warehouse anyways. Admit to the Z-team that you are Mecha Man, to the ire of Flambae? Well it doesn't matter because he will come around to you at the end of the next episode. Fail every single QTE? DOESN'T MATTER, the same thing always happens at the end of the fight. 

Why does AdHoc have to pretend that choices matter with the "X character will remember this" thing, when they could have just made Dispatch a web series where you play a mini game every now and then, like they clearly want to do? Would have certainly cut the costs down a bit. I'm not necessarily complaining about the illusion of choice, because at the end of the day, all entertainment media is an illusion that we choose to believe for the sake of not being bored. I'm just saying that AdHoc needs to either make a BETTER illusion of choice, or get rid of the illusion altogether. And I'm also saying this from a place of passion, because again, this game is very well written. All of the characters are like able and funny. The voice acting and animation is top notch. The mini game looks like a fun little management sim that allows for plenty of opportunities for character interactions.

Author: @callmev3531
Content:
Miscellaneous observations:

3:12, Andrew Arcadi's really shining in his work on the sound track.

3:51, Jack's earlier connection of each character's personalities to their special abilities works even better when comparing Toxic and Flambae, who besides their differing element, otherwise seem to have the exact same power set, 1:11:25, including flight and super-physicality by infusing themselves with their respective element to get these "super-modes". 

5:00, The scene also seems to suggest that most super-beings in general have some degree of super-physicality like in The Incredibles or The Boys, The Incredibles especially having a Stat-Ranking System that lists "Indestructibility" as an attribute for supers to have varying degrees of. That being said, Robert is still recovering from a months-long coma and was shown to be pretty super-abled even without powers or using his suit, 1:06:58, 1:07:13, 1:08:17, 1:09:15, and yet, when pushed, he is still extraordinarily resilient regardless.

7:15, The game's choice system is more-so based around Robert's personality and motivations, not the players, which is why there isn't an option to fight against cutting anyone, or not picking either Blazer or Invisigal, because in both instances, Robert trusts Blazer and wants to help Invisigal. It's up to the player merely how much Robert acts on his wants, not *what* he wants.

14:52, "HA....Got ee'm!" 59:36, Also, this laugh was so good.

21:33, I was wondering when someone would make this joke. Fitting it's Laura Bailey's character that did it.

26:04, 37:26, I was thinking that it just meant any attempt to use a certain stat with that Blocked Condition on it would result in automatic failure. In this case, attempting to use Combat to solve this problem would be an automatic failure.

28:37, 1:14:22, I'm curious of the politics around killing for heroes is in this setting. Besides mainstream comics, works like The Incredibles or Invincible have hero communities with unspoken leeway regarding killing as long as it's defensive and not an execution. The Incredibles especially has background lore regarding heroes that regularly kill, but got minimal public backlash for it like Gamma Jack and his casually lethal approach to killing criminals and villains. 55:08, 56:27, Dispatch's setting being so casual about it's fantastical and paranormal elements as for there to be establishments specifically for villains, as if they were just mere thugs in a biker gang, supports the idea that heroes killing is, to some degree, frowned upon, even if it may still happen. Just like heroes are  treated as celebrities or athletes, villains seem to be treated more like gangsters or mercenaries, only targeted when they've done an actual crime or have evidence implicating them in a crime, but otherwise are ignored by institutions charged with maintaining order.

33:07, 35:23, I genuinely thought this would be more like Die Hard 2 and a way it could be achieved would include illuminating a path for the pilots to land using light-generating supers like Flambae or Prism.

36:58, 38:31, Players I've seen with this game tend to neglect Malevola despite Healing Inducement being in her ability set due to her Life Transferal ability. Waterboy being another Healing Inducer only adds to that advantage.

56:31, The white-masked villain was the energy sword-wielder shooting bolts at Mecha Man in the first episode. 1:01:13, In fact, other of Shroud's goons are here, including the one that Mecha Man first choked out when infiltrating Shroud's base. This furthers the idea that villains in this setting are treated more like gangsters or mercenaries than they are terrorists.

1:10:44, Both Prism....5:50, and Flambae earlier....considering Mecha Man a "real superhero" is interesting because Prism in her ego and immature likely doesn't respect most people and Flambae outright dismissed Mecha Man the second time they met at Crypto Night. Flambae in particular mainly gives him any esteem later when he feels he can use it to make himself seem more impressive and lord it over Robert....just as he tries to use the fact that he's a super-being with powers to make himself seem superior to others. 1:11:52, The rest of the team contrast this by actually seeking connection and relatability as people, not trying to make themselves separate from or above each other through power or status. 1:55:33, Chase is also reflects Flambae's attitude of wanting to feel important, only he actually earned it by caring about actually helping others.

1:14:31, 1:54:15, I sort of doubt they're going in that direction with the twists. Shroud, for instance, is confirmed to be his own person, Elliot Connors, who made the Astral Pulse, but was neglected by the Brave Brigade, meaning he likely isn't Robert's father. Blazer has just been overwhelmed by the pressures of her corporate and celebrity status, and has been acting recklessly in increasingly short intervals due to her need to "shake shit up" and feel like a person instead of just a public icon or a corporate tool. 1:22:02, 2:08:00, But then again, more things could be done that validate these theories, and Invisigal did specifically enter the Phoenix Program on the condition her motives weren't questioned, motives that ostensibly are that she genuinely wants to be a hero, but is too afraid to give up the tough, amoral thug persona that defines her.

1:46:23, 1:48:06, So now Robert has *two* pervert super-beings gunning for him. It's like he's in an anime or something. 1:48:43, And as it turns out, Invisigal, who made fun of the band Phoenix, is playing a song from a band called Fart Barf.

Content:
being that i picked to keep zonar and add phenomaman to my team, it's very fun seeing the complete opposite of this in your gameplay. started watching you play, then picked up the game myself and chose those specifically to get to see that experience (loved phenomaman from the first episode, i love me a well meaning himbo. and my "i can fix him" pinged seeing him lie on that damn car. i just had to see more of him and get to know him a bit more. also cutting coupè means he's synergizeing with punch-up and that is a very fun dynamic, my heavy hitters).

Author: @marekfialka9046
Content:
Hey Jack just finished the chapters myself and well, I sure didn't expect to cry myself to sleep today 🥲.
Anyway here is my thory on who might've snitched/ planted a bug at Robert's place:

1) it can't be: 

• Coupé/Sonar - Has to be someone you can't cut, wouldn't be as impactful if a character you can fire 25% into the game and it's like "Hey, the guy you cut last week, yea he reached to us and had his buddy tell us the location." (Shit writing IMO and so far the writing has been a solid 9/10)
• Royd - dude genuinely wants to help and it shows, felt so sad when he didn't brofist me and just walked away thinking it was all his fault and that he's not good enough to help Robert💔💔 (even after I assured him)
• Waterboy/Phenomaman - also the player choice dilema, plus they are both written as good but flawed people, suddenly turning either one of them into a villain would be terrible writing (plus everybody is praising Phenomaman for not being an "evil Omniman/superman type hero" but rather their unique "depressed superman type hero")
• Golem - I mean the dude ain't even a villain, he's just getting a lot of shit for being big (but buy him a drink or two and you'll see the biggest smile under the sun), the worst thing he has done is vandalism whilst some ex-villains are in the Phoenix program after a history of assault, arson or murder; like Blazer said: he just want's a friend
• invisigal or Chase... obviously

2) it probably isn't but could be:

• Blazer - some folk theorize that she's Shroud's daughter, if true she could either resent her father so she tries to help heroes who have lost their jobs (and family) to villains like Robert and Chase (RIP legend) or she could be genuinelly working with Shroud to idk, create and control the chaos in LA to boost each other's profits or something like that, (honestly I'm like 90% positive the latter part is bs)
• Galen (the super hearing guy) - imagine if the whole time he was giving out some info to the villains for a slice of the profit, no one would even suspect this guy and he could've heard the dialogue from Robert house from miles away (again I'm like 80% sure this is bs, but a fun speculation regardless)

3) Could be:

• any other Z-team hero - either they could've been in the Phoenix program to gather info in the first place or they've ran into some villains during a dispatch offering an oppurtunity to make some extra cash (like planting bugs and selling info)

• Toxic (aka Soothing goon) - dude was first seen already INSIDE Robert's appartment, given how easily he got out from that heavy thing we used to crush him in Ep1 not to mention surviving getting stomped/yeeted by a couple ton mech suit BEFORE activating his powers proves he got captured willingly (I'm 100% sure on this). He likely got out of the dumpster, flew back into the appartment and planted a bug thinking Robert might one day discuss his plans out loud in his appartment (should they fail on that night's ambush, which they kinda did since they didn't get the pulse), had it not been for the surprise party all they would ever hear would be his drunken motivational speech or him talking to Beef. Honestly my money is on this!

PS: loved your voice performance and the jokes you cracked in these chapters 💚💚

Author: @Haydrik_osity
Content:
I don't think Blonde Blazer is working for Shroud... personally, I feel Blonde Blazer IS Shroud.

We see purple smoke when the Mecha Man Suit malfunctions, yet Robert comes out in one piece; while Royd ends up being somehow more harmed than Robert was. We see Shroud drop a smoke grenade on Invisigal; though with how dark it was and with the red light; I don't know if it was exactly PURPLE in color... but I feel it's no coincidence. It would give a possible reason for why Robert is alive. Maybe Blonde Blazer kept him alive for some reason to use as leverage, or to give a motive to track the Astral Pulse with Mecha Man still being alive and well enough to motivate the Z-Team to help towards rebuilding Mecha Man by getting the Pulse back.

If Bakugan taught me anything with the reveal of Masquerade; if they have a mask, anyone could be hiding beneath it. Shroud is often referred to as "He" or "His" and I feel that only motivates towards the possibility of confusing who Shroud really is. We see none of Shroud's body. Not their face, not their build, not anything. Shroud's name even points to the fact that their identity is concealed. I have my bets on Blonde Blazer being Shroud, and I have my doubts that she's just a henchman. She seems a bit too friendly towards Robert, and I have to believe there's a reason for that which goes beyond "helping that little scruffy superhero who just lost his job."

It could also explain all the failed tests. Maybe Blonde Blazer was sabotaging them? I don't know her full abilities, but she seems like an every-woman. Strong, Fast, Durable... I have to believe she'd probably be able to fly across the world and back in less than a couple seconds. Maybe I'm thinking too much; but I feel she has some dirt that we'll find out about soon.

It feels possible that she wanted to delay and make a plan because it'd work better; but it could also be so she could stop the Z-Team from interfering with her plan... but then again, it was specifically her that chose to keep Invisigal in Dispatch; so I assume she had a reason to keep a leash on her. Maybe because she'd be a threat, maybe because Invisigal could take the blame or take a fall for Blonde Blazer when she'd need it. Maybe it's because with Blonde Blazer knowing Invisigal's weakness being her Asthma that she saw her as an easy target to take down if she got in her way? The point is... I'm invested. :3

Author: @original_demonic
Content:
I love the fact that flambé rose above the hatred. It’s such an understated move and played for a joke after a heavy scene, but in a world where it would be so easy for him to just go back to his routine, hate Robbert, and say heroism is a scam, it does take a lot to actually want to better yourself.

He’s an asshole, but he’s someone who doesn’t exactly want to be one, and where it would have been easy to just have him go back to villainy, and he seems like the most douchbag one to do that, but he actually has subtle moments of character growth. Yeh, he’s pissed at his fingers being cut off, but after reflecting, he realises that now is what’s important, not back then. Being angry now about something when Robbert is actively trying to help, and told him who he was at the detriment of his own safety because he knew how Flambé would react, that’s taking the easy way out, and he doesn’t want to do that anymore, even if he is still an angry hothead.
